common_name: King Arthur Delphinium (Deep Violet-Blue with White Bee Pacific Giant)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; King Arthur is a classic Pacific Giant delphinium strain bearing deep violet-blue flowers with a contrasting white center (the 'bee').

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, staking tall flower spikes to protect them from wind and summer storms. King Arthur, one of the original named strains in the classic Pacific Giant delphinium series, produces towering spikes densely packed with large, semi-double, deep royal-violet-blue flowers, each centered with a contrasting white 'bee,' opening from the bottom of the spike upward over several weeks in early summer. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines quickly in summer heat and humidity, while in cooler zones it can persist as a short-lived perennial with excellent drainage and protection from wind. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut spent flower spikes back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible secondary round of shorter spikes later in the season.

Black Knight bears towering spikes of large, semi-double flowers in an intensely deep purple-black shade, among the darkest colors available in the classic Pacific Giant delphinium series, each flower centered with a small contrasting black 'bee' that nearly disappears into the dark petals. Its dramatic, moody color makes a striking vertical accent against paler companions in a cottage garden or cutting border. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines quickly in summer heat and humidity. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut spent flower spikes back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible secondary, shorter round of flowering later in the season.
